projects.name: Drake Meat Processors Saskatoon Processing Plant
projects.description: A new 53,000-square-foot meat processing facility under construction in Saskatoon, Saskatchewan, with capacity to produce over 17.6 million pounds of product annually. Supported by an equity investment.

evidence.title: Drake Meat Processors equity investment supports construction of Canada processing plant
evidence.snippet: A new 53,000-square-foot meat processing facility is under construction in Saskatoon, Saskatchewan, capable of producing over 17.6 million pounds of product annually.

projects.name: Atlantic Beef Products Halal Processing Expansion
projects.description: Atlantic Beef Products Inc. in Albany, PEI — the only federally registered beef processing plant east of Quebec — received up to $2,256,786 in federal funding under the Kosher and Halal Investment Program to install advanced steam vacuum systems, upgrade meat-recovery equipment, add new packaging technology, and implement an in-line x-ray analyzer to expand halal processing capacity.

evidence.title: Government of Canada invests in improved halal beef processing and packaging in Prince Edward Island
evidence.snippet: The Government of Canada announced an investment of up to $2,256,786 for Atlantic Beef Products Inc. on January 9, 2026.

evidence.title: Atlantic Beef Products receives $2.2M in federal funding to modernize operations
evidence.snippet: Atlantic Beef Products Inc. (ABPI), located in Albany, PEI, is the only federally registered beef processing plant east of Quebec.

projects.name: Atlas Engineered Products Advanced Wood Manufacturing Facility (Clinton, ON)
projects.description: A new advanced wood manufacturing facility in Clinton, Ontario, powered by advanced robotics to produce wooden trusses. The Government of Canada is contributing over $4 million under Natural Resources Canada's Investments in Forest Industry Transformation (IFIT) program.

evidence.title: Government of Canada supports new advanced wood manufacturing facility to strengthen Canada's construction supply chain
evidence.snippet: Atlas Engineered Products Ltd. will build a new, cutting-edge wood manufacturing facility, powered by advanced robotics, with over $4 million federal support.

projects.name: Kap Paper Kapuskasing MDF Facility Conversion
projects.description: Kap Paper Inc. in Kapuskasing, Ontario is pursuing conversion of its mill to a medium-density fibreboard (MDF) facility. The Government of Canada is investing $7.5 million (January 2026) through the Strategic Response Fund for a Front End Engineering Design study, bringing combined federal support to $17.5 million including $10 million announced October 2025. Plant conversion forecast at up to 30 months.

evidence.title: Government of Canada announces funding to support regional sawmills and employment in Northeast Ontario
evidence.snippet: The Government of Canada is investing $7.5 million through the Strategic Response Fund to help Kap Paper Inc. complete a FEED study toward a new MDF facility.

evidence.title: Ottawa funds engineering study to convert Kap Paper into fibreboard mill
evidence.snippet: The study will establish criteria for a final investment decision on creating a new MDF facility in Kapuskasing.

projects.name: 5 Wing Goose Bay Energy Performance Contract
projects.proponent: Department of National Defence / MCW Custom Energy Solutions Ltd.
projects.description: A $187 million Energy Performance Contract awarded to MCW Custom Energy Solutions Ltd. to modernize the Central Heating Plant at 5 Wing Goose Bay, replacing diesel systems with electric boilers powered by Labrador's hydroelectric grid. Part of long-term NORAD northern basing investments at the site totalling up to $8 billion. Construction begins May 2026, completion expected December 2030.

evidence.title: Minister Thompson announces largest Canadian defence investment in Newfoundland and Labrador's history
evidence.snippet: A $187 million Energy Performance Contract awarded to MCW Custom Energy Solutions Ltd.; construction begins May 2026, completion December 2030.

evidence.title: Largest Canadian defence investment in Newfoundland and Labrador
evidence.snippet: Up to $8 billion in long-term investments at 5 Wing Goose Bay; $187 million EPC to MCW Custom Energy Solutions.

projects.name: Woodland's Mihta Askiy Data Centre
projects.proponent: Woodland Cree First Nation / Sovereign Digital Infrastructure
projects.description: A proposed USD 1.5 billion data centre near Peace River, Alberta, developed by Woodland Cree First Nation in partnership with Sovereign Digital Infrastructure. Targeted for commissioning by 2027.

evidence.title: Largest Upcoming Data Centers in Canada 2026
evidence.snippet: Woodland's Mihta Askiy — Woodland Cree First Nation & Sovereign Digital Infrastructure — Peace River, Alberta — USD 1.5 billion — Planning — Commission by 2027.

projects.name: Beacon AI Centers High River Data Centre
projects.description: A proposed 400 MW data centre in Foothills County near High River, Alberta, a USD 4 billion project. Construction targeted for 2025-2026 with operations by 2030.

evidence.title: Largest Upcoming Data Centers in Canada 2026
evidence.snippet: Beacon AI Centers — Foothills County (High River), Alberta — USD 4 billion — Planned — Construction 2025-2026, operational by 2030.

projects.name: Hay River Water Treatment Plant
projects.description: A new water treatment plant in Hay River, Northwest Territories, replacing aging infrastructure that serves the town, the Hamlet of Enterprise, K'atl'odeeche First Nation and Ka'a'gee Tu First Nation. The federal government is contributing $20,138,995 through the Build Communities Strong Fund. Project to begin 2026-27.

evidence.title: Building Canada strong by investing in a new water treatment plant in Hay River
evidence.snippet: The federal government is investing $20,138,995 in this project through the Direct Delivery stream of the Build Communities Strong Fund.

projects.name: Red-Seine-Rat Cooperative Wastewater Treatment Facility
projects.description: A new $205 million wastewater treatment facility in Niverville, Manitoba, with construction contract awarded to Aecon (February 2026). Serves the municipalities of Niverville, Tache, Hanover, Ritchot, La Broquerie and De Salaberry — initially more than 30,000 people, with capacity for up to 70,000 residents.

evidence.title: Aecon awarded contract to build $205M wastewater treatment plant in Manitoba
evidence.snippet: Aecon has been awarded a contract for the Red-Seine-Rat Cooperative Wastewater Treatment Facility project in Niverville, Man. with a contract value of $205 million.

projects.name: Iqaluit Nukkiksautiit Hydroelectric Project
projects.description: A proposed 15-30 MW, 100% Inuit-owned hydroelectric facility on the Kuugaluk River (McKeand River South) near Iqaluit, Nunavut, intended to replace the city's diesel-generated electricity. The federal government is investing $6 million for engineering and design work. Project referred to the federal Major Projects Office; construction expected to begin 2028, operational by 2030.

evidence.title: Federal government invests $6M into Iqaluit hydro project
evidence.snippet: This project is 100 per cent Inuit-owned, and the federal government is investing $6 million into the hydro project for engineering and design work.

evidence.title: Iqaluit Nukkiksautiit Hydroelectric Project referred to the Major Projects Office
evidence.snippet: The Iqaluit Nukkiksautiit Hydroelectric Project, led by the Nunavut Nukkiksautiit Corporation, will advance planning for a hydroelectric facility near Iqaluit.

projects.name: Upper Afton Wind Project
projects.proponent: Government of Nova Scotia (environmental assessment approved)
projects.description: A wind farm to be built in Antigonish and Guysborough counties, Nova Scotia, with up to 28 eight-megawatt turbines. Received environmental assessment approval on April 22, 2026; construction expected to begin in 2027.

evidence.title: Upper Afton Wind Project Receives Environmental Assessment Approval
evidence.snippet: The Upper Afton Wind Project, to be built in Antigonish and Guysborough counties, received its environmental assessment approval on April 22, with up to 28 eight-megawatt turbines.
